Introduction

What Is an LLP?

A Limited Liability Partnership combines the flexibility of a partnership with limited liability protection for its partners. It's registered under the LLP Act, 2008, and is a separate legal entity from its partners, meaning personal assets stay protected from business liabilities.

LLPs suit professional service firms and small businesses that want limited liability without the higher compliance burden of a Private Limited Company.

Advantages & Disadvantages

Advantages

  • Limited liability protection for all partners
  • No minimum capital contribution required
  • Lower compliance burden than a Private Limited Company
  • Separate legal entity with perpetual succession
  • No cap on the number of partners

Disadvantages

  • Cannot raise equity funding the way a company can
  • Less familiar to some investors than a Private Limited Company
  • Still requires annual ROC filings (Form 11 and Form 8)
  • Conversion to a company later involves its own process

Eligibility

Who Can Register an LLP

  • Minimum 2 designated partners, with no upper limit
  • At least one designated partner must be resident in India
  • No minimum capital contribution requirement
  • A registered office address in India
  • Partners must have a valid DPIN and DSC

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

Obtain DSC for all designated partners — typically 1 working day.

2. Name Reservation

Apply for LLP name approval via the RUN-LLP service — 1 to 2 working days.

3. Incorporation Filing

File FiLLiP with the ROC along with subscriber and partner details.

4. LLP Agreement Filing

File the LLP Agreement (Form 3) within the prescribed timeline after incorporation.

5. Certificate of Incorporation

Once approved, you receive the Certificate of Incorporation — typically within 10–15 working days overall. Timelines can vary based on ROC processing.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN card of all designated partners
  • Aadhaar / address proof of all partners
  • Passport-size photographs
  • Proof of registered office (utility bill + NOC from owner)
  • Rent agreement, if applicable

Annual Compliance

Ongoing Requirements After Registration

  • Annual Return filing (Form 11)
  • Statement of Accounts & Solvency (Form 8)
  • Income tax return filing
  • Tax audit, if turnover exceeds the applicable threshold
  • Maintenance of the LLP Agreement and partner records

Common Mistakes to Avoid

What Trips Up New LLPs

  • Delaying the LLP Agreement filing beyond the prescribed timeline
  • Assuming LLPs have no annual filing requirement
  • Not updating the agreement when partners or contributions change
  • Missing the Form 11 deadline each year
